correctness.rationale: For every fixed positive m, unique gcd normalization yields an exact floor sum. The number of candidate primitive pairs below sqrt(mX) is O_m(X), bounding all floor errors. Möbius inversion reduces the weighted primitive congruence sum to arithmetic-progression harmonic sums, whose uniform Riemann-sum error is O(1/v); absolute convergence yields O_d(1) in the logarithmic summation formula. The Euler product is evaluated prime by prime and gives C_m. A standalone verifier checks exact counts via two different implementations; finite tests are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem evaluates a natural global first-moment invariant of the precise graphs appearing in the Erdős–Graham problem, where recent work studies large independent subsets. It sharpens a known O(X log X) harmonic-triple counting scale to an exact leading coefficient and provides a nontrivial multiplicative law across all fixed divisibility parameters. The ratio 4/3 directly compares the two original sibling divisibility relations. This has value independently of a solution to the hard extremal independence problem.
